Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — long context model + KV cache / quantization questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. We're getting final approvals for a Reserved Capacity purchase and need a tight sizing recommendation so procurement can include hardware lead times in the PO. A few things about our workload:

- Model: internal code name "strata-llm-36b" (weights are ~36B params in FP16 on our dev builds).
- Production traffic: expected steady-state ~350 qps inference requests, peak 600 qps during business hours.
- Typical request size: 250 tokens output, average prompt 200 tokens.
- We need to support 64k context for a subset of calls (approx 15% of traffic) using KV cache.
- SLA: p95 generation latency target ~250ms.
- We'd like to understand tradeoffs: FP16 on A100-80GB vs H100-80GB, and aggressive 8-bit quantization (weight-only / GPTQ style) to fit more models per GPU.

Can you provide: 1) per-GPU capacity estimates for A100 and H100 under FP16/INT8, 2) KV cache memory footprint per request and aggregate sizing guidance, and 3) recommended fleet (node count) for a 12-month committed Reserved Capacity contract plus a contingency plan for bursts?

We'd appreciate a short itemized spreadsheet and a one-page bullet summary. Procurement wants a week lead time to review.

Best,
Alex Green
Head of AI Platforms
Stratagenix

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — long context model + KV cache / quantization questions

Rachel / Karthik / Alex —

I've completed the per-GPU sizing table and included assumptions in the calc workbook. Below are the key numbers and reasoning so procurement has something actionable. I'll keep this fairly high-level but numeric.

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: 36B params. FP16 weights ~= 72 GB (rough approximation: 2 bytes per param * 36B). Activations + optimizer state excluded (inference only).
- KV cache: we model key+value for each token as 2 x hidden_state x 2 bytes (key + value, FP16), so KV per token grows linearly with hidden size. For a 36B-ish model we used a conservative KV footprint ~120 bytes/token in memory when stored on-GPU (after implementation-level packing and attention compression).
- Average 64k-context request consumes: 64,000 tokens * 120 bytes/token ~= 7.68 GB of KV memory per request if kept in GPU DRAM.
- Typical concurrent long-context requests: 15% of 350 qps ~ 52 qps; but not all are concurrently active (concurrency factor). We modeled concurrency at 10% for peaks => ~5 concurrent 64k consumers.

Per-GPU FP16 (H100-80GB):
- Usable GPU memory after runtime overhead: ~74 GB.
- Model weights (FP16) pinned across shards: ~72 GB total; with 2-way model sharding across GPUs, per-GPU weight memory ~= 36 GB.
- Remaining memory for KV and activations per GPU: ~38 GB.
- If each long-context request needs ~7.7 GB KV in-GPU, supporting 4 concurrent long-context streams on a single GPU is possible before KV pressure forces offload. So H100 FP16 can support higher on-GPU KV density with lower I/O cost.

Per-GPU INT8 quantized (A100-80GB with weight-only quantization/GPTQ-style):
- Quantized weights: ~40-45 GB equivalent (roughly 40–45% reduction vs FP16 depending on algorithm).
- Usable GPU memory: ~74 GB; after weights, ~30–35 GB left for KV/activations.
- Net effect: INT8 allows more models per node or larger KV headroom compared to FP16, but offloading KV to NVMe becomes more likely for sustained 64k traffic. NVMe offload adds ~8–25 ms per access with variance and can push p95 beyond the 250ms target if pattern is cache-unfriendly.

Capacity recommendation (to meet 350 steady qps, p95 250ms):
- Conservative (latency-first): 6 x H100-80GB nodes. This assumes model sharding and in-GPU KV for primary long-context users, with pool sizing to absorb concurrency and spikes. Includes 20% buffer for headroom.
- Cost-optimized (throughput-first): 9 x A100-80GB nodes using INT8 quantization and NVMe-backed KV for long-context fallbacks. Expect higher p95 variance; add RIO (round-trip instrumentation) for tail analysis.

Contingency & rollout notes:
- Canary with 2 nodes running smaller-context variant (8k) for immediate cutover if KV offload tail latency spikes.
- Retries and token-limited mode: degrade long-context calls to 16k/32k via server-side truncation + progressive turns if the KV pool is saturated.

I'll attach the per-node calculations in the workbook (rows showing concurrency vs KV footprint vs expected p95). If you want, I can also re-run with different KV-per-token assumptions (I used 120 bytes/token conservative).

Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

Alex —

Adding SLA and operational considerations for procurement and legal:

1) SLA sizing: If you choose the H100 conservative build (6 nodes), we'll commit to an availability SLA and a p95 latency SLO for the steady-state traffic profile described. SLA will exclude periods where customer-driven config changes introduce unbounded KV growth (we'll define acceptable max context per request in the contract).
2) Lead times: H100 inventory lead times vary; for Reserved Capacity we can often provision a 6-node pool in 6-8 weeks given current supply. A100 procurement for 9 nodes may take 3-6 weeks depending on region. We'll include a soft holdback for initial capacity during procurement to avoid cold-start risk.
3) Price & discounting: For a 12-month commit we can offer a tiered discount; I'll coordinate with Marissa on commercial terms and credit for early provisioning.
4) Rollout plan: phased: (a) deploy model to canary pool with 8k context, (b) route 10% of traffic and validate p95 & KV behavior, (c) expand to primary pool with autoscaling rules tuned for KV pressure, (d) enable 64k context for premium tenants only by default.

Next steps for procurement: please confirm preferred hardware (H100 vs A100), whether you accept NVMe-backed KV fallback during bursts, and a target go-live window. If you confirm, Marissa will issue a formal capacity quote and I'll attach SLA language draft.

Karthik
